_doc: Hand-authored base scenarios for core_capability_stacking_regression. Each scenario is an office-automation job needing 2-4 tool calls, ALL of which are satisfied by skills in catalog.json's `base` set -- stacking never removes the right answer, it only adds neighbours. `expected_args` lists only the arguments the request objectively determines; every one of them must be marked `required` in the correct tool's own schema, which build_cases.py asserts, so the judge can never penalise an omission the schema did not ask for. `unchecked_required` records the required arguments deliberately NOT checked because their value is free-form prose (a subject line, a message body, a row's cell text) -- verifying prose deterministically needs an LLM judge, which this task avoids. That is a real scoring looseness and it is recorded here rather than hidden. No request text may contain the name of a correct tool; build_cases.py asserts that too. `difficulty` decides whether a scenario can enter the primary test: only `medium` and `hard` do (grader.py PRIMARY_TIERS). The `easy` tier states its disqualifying constraint in the request text and is a harness canary; L0 is already the per-scenario floor check, so the easy tier is kept deliberately small.
